in_arrest_no_charges.publicName: Clearing an arrest where you were never charged
in_arrest_no_charges.venue: A circuit or superior court in the county where the charges or allegation were filed, or where the arrest occurred if none were filed.

destination.name: Circuit or superior court in the county of filing or arrest
destination.detail: The court serves a copy of the petition on the prosecuting attorney under § 35-38-9-1(f). No filing fee.

rules.filing: File the verified petition, order, appearance where self-represented, Notice of Exclusion and Confidential Information Form with a circuit or superior court in the county where the charges were filed, or where the arrest occurred if none were filed.
rules.fees: None. Section 1 petitions carry no filing fee.
rules.feeWaiver: Not applicable. There is no fee.
rules.notice: The court serves a copy of the petition on the prosecuting attorney under § 35-38-9-1(f). The court shall grant unless the subsection (a) conditions are unmet or criminal charges are pending, and may summarily deny a petition that shows on its face that the person is not entitled to relief.
rules.service: The court serves the prosecuting attorney. The CCA appearance form nonetheless carries a certificate of service to the county prosecutor; follow the form.
rules.participantSignature: The petition is verified and signed by the petitioner.

waitingPeriods.condition: The arrest, with no charges pending

packetInstructions: Never say records are destroyed. In Indiana expungement means records are sealed or restricted under § 35-38-9-1(k). The Office of Judicial Administration states plainly that court records are not deleted or destroyed under I.C. 35-38-9.

Put only the last four digits of the Social Security number on the petition. The full number goes on the Confidential Information Form, filed as a confidential document, accompanied by the Notice of Exclusion of Confidential Information from Public Access. Do not persist the full number.
Disclose that the expungement case file is public until the order is granted.
Tell the participant plainly that expungement does not shorten the statute of limitations and the prosecutor may still file a charge later.
The court serves the prosecuting attorney under § 35-38-9-1(f). The participant does not serve, although the appearance form carries its own certificate of service; follow the form.
selfHelpStopConditions: The prosecutor objects or files a notice in opposition.
A victim submits a statement in opposition.
The court sets a hearing.
The person has convictions in more than one county and the 365-day window is already partly consumed.
A conviction is not yet eligible and the person wants to file now, which is the Chastain trap.
The person has already filed a Sections 2 through 5 petition.
Classification between Sections 2, 3, 4 and 5 is unclear, or turns on whether an offence caused serious bodily injury.
The person is a sex or violent offender or subject to registration.
Fines, fees, costs or restitution are unpaid or disputed.
Charges are pending anywhere, or the person is in a pretrial diversion programme.
The record involves a commercial driver's licence and 49 C.F.R. 384.226.
Immigration, firearm, licensing or CDL consequences are in play.
The person wants to attack the underlying conviction rather than expunge it.
